ActivityCursor.description:
A position in one lease's event stream.

A sequence is meaningless without the lease it counts within, so the two
travel together and "no position yet" is the absence of a cursor rather
than a sequence of zero paired with a missing lease.
ActivityCursor.title: ActivityCursor

BlockingCondition.description: Why the WorkUnit is not moving, in the terms an operator can act on.
BlockingCondition.title: BlockingCondition

BrowserAcceptanceView.description: The browser-acceptance profile as the project row publishes it.
BrowserAcceptanceView.title: BrowserAcceptanceView

DispatchIntentStatus.description:
Every state a dispatch intent can occupy.

DispatchTerminalStatus names only the two an executor reports back. This is
the full column vocabulary, which is what a reader or a comparison needs.
DispatchIntentStatus.title: DispatchIntentStatus

EventView.description:
One domain event, in the shape both the view and the events route return.

``extra="forbid"`` is the point of this model existing rather than a dict: a
field added to ``repository.event_to_payload`` and not added here fails
validation loudly instead of vanishing from the HTTP contract.
EventView.title: EventView

ExecutionEventEntry.description:
One durable lifecycle event, as the cockpit renders it.

A ledger row carries more than a timeline row shows, and it will carry more
again. `from_ledger_row` names every column this view depends on, so the
dependency is visible and a new ledger column cannot reach the cockpit by
accident or break it on arrival.
ExecutionEventEntry.title: ExecutionEventEntry

ExecutionLiveness.description: Whether a durable execution is still being carried by anything.
ExecutionLiveness.title: ExecutionLiveness

ExecutionRecoveryView.description:
What a resume had to repair before it could continue anything.

An operator otherwise cannot tell "this continued a run that parked for me"
from "this recovered a run that crashed", because both return the same
accepted resume. ``halted_epoch`` is the epoch whose death had gone
unrecorded, and ``null`` whenever nothing needed repairing.
ExecutionRecoveryView.title: ExecutionRecoveryView

ExhaustedMilestoneView.description:
A milestone the resume refused to try again, and the arithmetic behind it.

An operator asking "why is this still blocked after I resumed it" needs the
numbers, not a sentence. ``override_request_id`` names the decision they can
answer to lift it, so the refusal carries its own remedy.
ExhaustedMilestoneView.title: ExhaustedMilestoneView

IntentFacts.description:
One dispatch intent, for the window before any lease exists.

Deliberately smaller than ``LeaseFacts``. An intent has no agent, no
supervisor, and no persistence lane, and the previous flattened shape made the
cockpit render four empty rows claiming otherwise.
IntentFacts.title: IntentFacts

LeaseFacts.description: One agent execution lease, as the cockpit renders it.
LeaseFacts.title: LeaseFacts

LifecyclePhase.description:
The fixed, ordered lifecycle phases.

Declaration order is the execution order. ``ORDERED_PHASES`` derives from it
so a reordered member cannot leave a second list saying otherwise.
LifecyclePhase.title: LifecyclePhase

OperatorDecision.description:
The wire spelling of an operator's answer.

Kept because it is what HTTP carries and what the decision row stores. It is
deliberately *not* what the lifecycle reasons about: on its own it cannot say
which kind of request it belongs to, so an `ANSWERED` and an `APPROVED` are
interchangeable to any code holding one. `decision_outcome` turns this into
the typed pairing below at the one boundary where the two are both known.
OperatorDecision.title: OperatorDecision

ProjectActionKind.description: Mutually exclusive operator actions projected by the project cockpit.
ProjectActionKind.title: ProjectActionKind

ProjectActionSnapshot.description: One deterministic, versioned answer to: what should the operator do next?
ProjectActionSnapshot.title: ProjectActionSnapshot

ProjectActivityPage.description: One bounded step through the current lease's lifecycle events.
ProjectActivityPage.title: ProjectActivityPage

ProjectCenterView.description: The project registry, as the cockpit's project picker reads it.
ProjectCenterView.title: ProjectCenterView

ProjectFacts.description: The registered project, including the two facts the action logic gates on.
ProjectFacts.title: ProjectFacts

ProjectStatusRow.description:
One registered project, with its git state when the path is a repository.

The git fields are absent from the underlying row when git was not consulted,
the path does not exist, or reading it failed. They are modelled as nullable
rather than optional so the published contract is "always present, sometimes
null", which is what a client actually receives once the model serializes.
ProjectStatusRow.title: ProjectStatusRow

StatusLegendEntry.description: One status: the token, what it means, and whose move it is.
StatusLegendEntry.title: StatusLegendEntry

StatusLegendView.description: The whole legend, one section per status vocabulary the cockpit renders.
StatusLegendView.title: StatusLegendView

StopAttemptView.description: One thing cancellation tried to stop, as the cockpit sees it.
StopAttemptView.title: StopAttemptView

StopTargetKind.description:
What sort of thing the cascade tried to stop.

A sum rather than a boolean pair because these fail for unrelated reasons and
an operator's next move differs: a refused intent may mean an agent is still
running, while a refused workflow means recovery could restart something.
StopTargetKind.title: StopTargetKind

StopVerdict.description:
What became of one attempt to stop something.

Three states rather than a boolean, because stopping an agent is not
synchronous and a boolean would have to lie in one direction or the other.
A lease that has been asked to cancel is neither stopped nor refused: a
supervisor will terminate its process group at the next heartbeat. Calling
that `True` claims the process is dead; calling it `False` reads as a failure
the operator must act on. It is a third thing, and it maps to a third
operator response, which is to wait a moment and re-check.
StopVerdict.title: StopVerdict

ValidationStatus.description:
The three outcomes of compiling, which are genuinely different.

``VALID`` may execute. ``BLOCKED`` compiled cleanly but names an unresolved
condition that must be answered first. ``INVALID`` never becomes executable
without editing the document.
ValidationStatus.title: ValidationStatus

WorkUnitDecisionRequest.description:
One operator decision, naming exactly the request it resolves.

``request_id`` is required. A decision that does not name a persisted request
cannot unblock anything, which is what keeps an approving-sounding message from
acting as an approval. ``idempotency_key`` makes a re-delivered submission
harmless.
WorkUnitDecisionRequest.title: WorkUnitDecisionRequest

WorkUnitDecisionResult.description:
What submitting one operator decision did.

``applied`` false with a ``reason`` is the idempotent case: the request was
already resolved, and saying so is not an error.
WorkUnitDecisionResult.title: WorkUnitDecisionResult

WorkUnitEventPage.description:
A forward-only window into the append-only history.

The cursor is the caller's own ``after_sequence``; there is no server cursor,
because WorkUnit sequence numbers are dense and monotonic within one WorkUnit.
WorkUnitEventPage.title: WorkUnitEventPage

WorkUnitExecutionResult.description: The root workflow's own report, returned only when it ran in-process.
WorkUnitExecutionResult.title: WorkUnitExecutionResult

WorkUnitResumeResult.description:
Whether a resume was accepted, and by what.

``delivered`` false is a real answer rather than a failure: no durable runtime
was available to take the continuation, so nothing was started.
WorkUnitResumeResult.title: WorkUnitResumeResult

WorkUnitSummary.description: One row of the WorkUnit list: enough to choose one, not enough to work it.
WorkUnitSummary.title: WorkUnitSummary

get.description:
Meaning and operator next-move for every status token the cockpit renders.

A constant, and served anyway: the legend must describe the statuses this
server emits, and a copy checked into the web bundle would drift from
them at the first mismatched deploy.
